articles.title: Simone Biles reveals the surprising relationship she has with an influencer
articles.standfirst: A simple request about a hairstylist ended with the Olympic champion deciding to hit unfollow
articles.summary: A simple request about a hairstylist ended with the Olympic champion deciding to hit unfollow
articles.body:
Simone Biles has never been shy about discussing the pressures that come with being one of the world's most recognizable athletes.

But in a recent story, the Olympic champion revealed an unexpectedly awkward relationship with an influencer that had nothing to do with gymnastics , and everything to do with hair.

Biles opened up about what she described as the “weirdest interaction” she had with an influencer a couple of years ago. The gymnast explained that she had followed the woman for some time because she admired her style and content, particularly the way she wore her hair.

The detail that caught Biles ' attention was how consistently polished the influencer's hairstyle appeared. Biles said it was always “laid to a T,” leaving her unsure whether the look was her natural hair or a weave.

At the time, Biles was particularly conscious about her own hair because of the criticism she had received online. That scrutiny had become a recurring issue throughout her career, including during major competitions.

“I didn’t really give a f**k that much. Y’all had been bullying me for so long about what my hair looked like during competition,” she recalled.

The criticism had nevertheless made Biles consider whether changing her hairstyle might quiet some of the comments. Because she already had conversations with the influencer about hair and had regularly complimented her looks, she felt comfortable asking for the contact details of her stylist.

“Girl, you need to send me your hair person contact slash Insta,” Biles recalled asking.

The response was not what she expected. According to Biles, the influencer told her, “My manager has it. I’ll have to ask her.”

That answer left the gymnast confused. She questioned why someone would not have the direct details of the person responsible for their hair.

“You don’t know who does your hair when you go to your hair appointments? You don’t have their contact or Instagram?” she asked in the video.

Biles acknowledged that she could understand someone wanting to protect a stylist's information. However, she said that was not what she had in mind.

“That’s not at all what it was, like I travel all the time, so if I’m ever in that area, let me get slay,” she said.

Rather than pursuing the matter, Biles ultimately decided that the interaction was not worth the negativity.

“But yeah, I didn’t need that kind of negativity in my life, so I unfollowed her,” Biles said.

Why hair has become such a personal subject for Biles

The incident was amusing enough for Biles to revisit years later, but it also connects to a much more serious part of her relationship with public scrutiny.

Biles has repeatedly faced criticism over her hair despite becoming one of the most decorated gymnasts in history. During the 2024 Paris Olympics, for example, she responded directly to social-media users who criticized her hairstyle.

She explained that the extreme heat and lengthy bus journey had affected her appearance before competition.

Her experiences have also shaped the way she views her natural hair. In a 2024 interview with Elle, Biles explained that she had gradually become more comfortable with her texture and the styles she could wear: “I used to worry about [my hair being considered] not professional. But I’m not embarrassed about it anymore.”

She has also spoken about growing up without learning to style her own hair, meaning professional hairstylists became an important part of her routine as her gymnastics career developed.

That history makes the influencer story particularly revealing. What started as Biles simply admiring another woman's hairstyle was connected to years of being told, directly and indirectly, how her own appearance should look.

Biles has previously argued that the scrutiny surrounding Black women's hair can become excessive. During the Paris Olympics, she famously pushed back against critics, telling them not to comment on a Black woman's hair while she was competing.

Her relationship with hair has continued to evolve away from trying to satisfy those expectations. More recently, she has also worked with K18 as a brand ambassador, with the partnership focusing on maintaining healthy hair despite the demands of training, traveling and performing.

The influencer episode therefore represents a lighter chapter in a much bigger story. Biles was not looking for anything complicated, she admired someone's hair, wanted the stylist's contact information and thought it could be useful when traveling.

Instead, the answer surprised her enough that she chose to walk away from the relationship. Years later, she still remembers the exchange.

“To this day, I still think about it, and it cracks me up, but it also like, what?” she said.

For someone who has spent much of her life under an extraordinary level of public scrutiny, the story is another example of Biles deciding which conversations deserve her attention, and which ones are better left behind.

articles.title: Simone Biles asked a simple question and got an answer she never expected
articles.standfirst: The Olympic legend admired the influencer and only wanted one simple favor, but the response was enough for Biles to unfollow her
articles.summary: The Olympic legend admired the influencer and only wanted one simple favor, but the response was enough for Biles to unfollow her
articles.body:
S imone Biles has dealt with pressure on the biggest stages in sports, but years later, one surprisingly small interaction with an influencer still leaves her wondering what exactly happened.

The 29-year-old gymnastics legend took to TikTok to tell the story of what she described as one of the "weirdest" interactions she has ever had with an influencer and how a simple question about hair eventually convinced her to hit the unfollow button.

Biles explained that the two had followed each other on social media for some time. She liked the woman's style and content, but there was one thing that particularly caught her attention: her hair always looked perfect.

And for Biles, that wasn't just about appearance.

Simone Biles explains why hair became such a sensitive subject

Throughout her career, Biles has faced relentless comments about her hair while competing, something she directly referenced while telling the story.

"Y'all have been bullying me for so long about what my hair looks like during competition," Biles said, explaining why she had become particularly interested in finding someone who could help her achieve the look she wanted.

That criticism wasn't something Biles imagined. During the Paris Olympics in 2024, she publicly responded to people commenting on her hair after competing with a ponytail, explaining that extreme heat and a long bus ride without air conditioning had affected how it looked.

So when Biles saw the influencer repeatedly posting photos with what she considered flawless hair, she eventually decided to ask.

The two had already exchanged messages about their hair when another Instagram Story gave Biles the opportunity. She complimented the influencer and asked for the contact information or Instagram account of the person who did her hair.

The response was not what she expected.

The answer that made Simone Biles say 'What?'

According to Biles, the influencer replied that her manager had the hairstylist's information and that she would have to ask her . Biles couldn't understand it.

"You don't know who does your hair when you go to your hair appointments?" she recalled thinking.

For Biles, it felt like unnecessary gatekeeping. She also pointed out that the two women didn't even live in the same state, making the idea that she might somehow take the influencer's hairstylist away from her even harder to understand.

Biles said her intention was much simpler. Because she travels frequently, she wanted the contact so she could potentially get her hair done whenever she happened to be in that area.

But she wasn't going to push the issue.

"I didn't need that kind of negativity in my life, so I unfollowed her," Biles said.

Years later, Biles still doesn't know whether the influencer was actually trying to protect her hairstylist, simply didn't have the contact information or whether there was another explanation entirely.

She only knows that the answer felt strange enough at the time to make her walk away. And apparently, strange enough that she still laughs about it today.

articles.title: "Why Not?": Jordan Chiles enlists Michael Jordan for epic LA 2028 comeback announcement
articles.standfirst: The Team USA star has ended months of uncertainty and confirmed she is chasing a third Games
articles.summary: The Team USA star has ended months of uncertainty and confirmed she is chasing a third Games
articles.body:
Jordan Chiles spent much of the past year refusing to rush the biggest decision of her gymnastics career. Now she has made it.

The two-time Olympian has confirmed she plans to pursue a place on Team USA for the 2028 Los Angeles Games , setting up the possibility of a third Olympic appearance four years after the medal controversy that overshadowed the end of her Paris campaign.

Chiles revealed the decision in a stylized announcement filmed in Los Angeles, with model Winnie Harlow and singer Normani appearing alongside her and Michael Jordan providing the voiceover.

“Why again? Because the dream is still there. Why continue? Because there’s still more to give,” Jordan says in the video. “Why now? Because not every chapter ends when people expect it to.”

He then asks why Chiles would return for a third attempt. Her answer is immediate: “Why not?” The 25-year-old completes the reveal by showing off a jeweled grill reading “LA 2028.”

Chiles deliberately kept Olympic future open

The announcement ends months of uncertainty around whether Chiles would continue at the elite level after completing her college career with UCLA.

Earlier this year, she made clear that another Olympic run would only happen if she felt physically and mentally ready.

“The biggest thing right now is just making sure my body and my mind are okay,” Chiles said. “I did give myself a deadline on when I would decide. So it’s not a yes, it’s not a no.”

That careful approach followed an extraordinary stretch in which Chiles balanced NCAA gymnastics, television appearances and the aftermath of the Paris Olympics.

At UCLA, she finished as a four-time NCAA champion and 23-time All-American before transitioning into a student coaching role for the 2027 season. Her elite resume is already substantial.

Chiles won team silver at the Tokyo Olympics and team gold in Paris, while also collecting World Championship medals and becoming one of the most recognizable figures in American gymnastics.

Paris medal battle still hangs over career

The most painful chapter of Chiles ’ Olympic story remains unresolved. She was initially awarded bronze in the floor exercise final in Paris after a U.S. scoring inquiry raised her mark.

Romania successfully challenged the timing of that inquiry, and Chiles was later ordered to return the medal.

The case has continued through the Swiss legal system, with Switzerland’s highest court directing the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reconsider the dispute after new audiovisual evidence was presented.

“This case is bigger than one competition or one result,” Chiles later wrote. “It is about trust.”

That experience could have made Paris feel like a natural endpoint. Instead, Chiles is choosing to write another chapter. With Los Angeles hosting the next Summer Games, the opportunity carries a different weight.

Suni Lee, Jade Carey and Hezly Rivera have also signaled their intention to pursue 2028, potentially setting up another fiercely competitive U.S. selection process. Chiles , however, has already answered the first question. She is coming back.

articles.title: Simone Biles gets "betrayed" by friend amidst Sophie Cunningham and Riley Gaines drama
articles.standfirst: The fallout from Cunningham's comments on transgender athletes continues.
articles.summary: The fallout from Cunningham's comments on transgender athletes continues.
articles.body:
She may not have intended it, but Sophie Cunningham truly opened a can of worms with her comments on the transgender athletes in women's sports debate. There's been no shortage of backlash and ensuing debate since her statement on the matter on July 22 .

This is far from the first time notable professional athletes have participated in discourse surrounding the transgender athletes topic, though. Just last summer, Olympics legend Simone Biles got into it with Riley Gaines , a former NCAA swimming All-American who has turned into a right-wing political activist.

During their exchange, Biles called her out as a " sore loser " who bullies young athletes, followed by Gaines saying the gymnast is a " male apologist ". The transgender topic has completely divided opinions within the sports space. And Cunningham has only made everything more polarized as of late.

Sophie Cunningham has divided people, even pro athletes, with her comments

Given the renewed emphasis on the topic, Biles and Gaines are once again in the spotlight . A recent video surfaced where Biles met up with Indiana Fever players, including Cunningham. Gaines over-analyzed the interaction between Biles and Cunningham, saying that the gymnast treated the WNBA player differently due to her comments .

Not letting go of the topic and their past feud, a friend of Gaines has added more fuel to the fire, directly commenting on Biles' interaction with Cunningham and delving into Biles' acquaintance at the game.

She looked less than enthused to see Sophie... The media doesn’t really know, but the guy she was sitting next to at the game posted this online, totally outing her and throwing her under the bus. She was sat next to a guy named Michael Buckley. ​ ​He posted this on his Instagram story the next day following the game: “I said to Simone last night, notice it’s always the mediocre white women who are complaining about trans athletes, and never the black women who are historically the best athletes. We were fired up. ​ ​He just absolutely outs her and reinforced her stance on how she feels about men and women’s sports.

That's a lot of projecting about how Biles truly feels, but this probably won't be the last time we hear from both Biles and Gaines on the matter.

articles.title: Simone Biles helps Suni Lee in her return to gymnastics after her mental health struggles
articles.standfirst: The Olympic champions reconnect as Lee takes another step toward returning to competitive gymnastics
articles.summary: The Olympic champions reconnect as Lee takes another step toward returning to competitive gymnastics
articles.body:
Simone Biles has once again shown her support for Suni Lee as the Olympic champion continues rebuilding her gymnastics career following a challenging period away from competition.

Lee recently gave fans another glimpse of her comeback by sharing training footage on Instagram. The 23-year-old gymnast was seen working across several events, including balance beam, uneven bars and vault.

Her session featured controlled drills, flips and difficult skills as she continues rebuilding the consistency and confidence required at the elite level.

She captioned the update, “back into the swing of thinggss!! some fun gym updates & progress for you guys.”

The footage is another encouraging moment in a comeback Lee officially announced in July. After stepping away from competition following the 2024 Paris Olympics, she confirmed that she’s returning to training with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in mind.

“I know what I’m capable of,” Lee said when announcing her comeback, adding that she was prepared to do whatever it takes to reach another Games.

Lee’s journey has involved more than simply taking time away from gymnastics because in 2023 she was diagnosed with two kidney diseases, forcing her to temporarily step away from the sport.

She eventually returned to competition and went on to win three medals at Paris 2024, including team gold and bronze medals in the all-around and uneven bars.

Biles has already helped Lee through a difficult moment

Biles ’ support for Lee has a particularly meaningful history. During the 2024 U.S. Championships, Lee had a difficult vault and walked into a tunnel to regain her composure. Biles went to check on her and offered reassurance based partly on her own experience with the “twisties” at the Tokyo Olympics.

Lee later said Biles helped restore her confidence, while Biles explained that she understood what Lee was experiencing and wanted her teammate to trust her gymnastics again. Biles even stayed nearby while Lee competed on uneven bars, where Lee responded with a strong routine.

Now, Biles has offered another small show of encouragement. After Lee posted her latest training footage, Biles commented with two tea emojis. A fan then jokingly replied to Biles , “Your turn,” referencing the possibility of her own return.

That possibility remains unresolved. In April 2026, Biles said she was still “50-50” on competing at the 2028 Olympics, explaining that mental health would play a major role in her decision.

Lee is the one actively working toward Los Angeles. Each new training clip offers another indication that she’s gradually finding her rhythm again.

With Biles continuing to cheer her on, their Olympic connection remains just as strong away from the competition floor.

articles.title: From setbacks to gold: Simone Biles melts hearts with nostalgic photos from early days in gymnastics
articles.standfirst: Biles reveals the imperfect beginning behind her historic gymnastics career
articles.summary: Biles reveals the imperfect beginning behind her historic gymnastics career
articles.body:
Simone Biles has spent years being measured by medals, difficulty scores and the boundaries she has pushed in gymnastics. On National Gymnastics Day, she chose to highlight something far simpler: the little girl who was still learning how to put a routine together.

Biles shared some of her oldest gymnastics videos, showing early attempts that were far removed from the precision fans now associate with her. The clips included falls, awkward landings and visible frustration, accompanied by a message aimed at young athletes.

“Kids, don’t ever give up on your dreams, this is where I started… happy national gymnastics day,” Biles wrote. Another clip came with a more playful caption: “*salutes, *picks wedgie, *falls, *pout, *picks wedgie again, *stomps off.”

The humor gave the post much of its charm. One of the greatest gymnasts ever was reminding people that her journey started with the same imperfections familiar to almost every child learning a sport.

From beginner to global star

Biles first encountered gymnastics at age six during a daycare field trip to a gym. What began as an introduction soon became a serious pursuit.

She qualified for the Women’s Junior Olympic National Championships in 2010, moved into elite competition the following year and, by 2013, had won the world all-around title in Antwerp at just 16.

That breakthrough began one of the most remarkable runs in gymnastics history.

Biles collected world titles through 2014 and 2015 before making her Olympic debut in Rio in 2016. She left those Games with four gold medals, team, all-around, vault and floor exercise, plus bronze on balance beam.

Her medal total eventually reached 11 at the Olympics, with Paris 2024 providing another defining chapter as she won team, all-around and vault gold and silver on floor.

“I’m not the next Usain Bolt or Michael Phelps,” Biles famously said during her rise. “I’m the first Simone Biles.”

Message means more after difficult chapters

Biles ’ career has never been only about dominance. At the Tokyo Olympics, she withdrew from several events after experiencing the “twisties,” placing athlete mental health at the center of a global conversation.

She later returned to win bronze on balance beam before rebuilding toward another Olympic run. Her future in the sport remains open.

Biles said in 2025 that she would attend the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics whether she competed or not. By May 2026, she described the chances of another comeback as “about 50 per cent.”

“I’ve already been to three Olympic Games, and I feel fulfilled,” she said. “It’s crazy to see how people always want more and more from you. In the end, the decision will always be mine.”

That's what makes the childhood footage resonate. It shows that greatness did not begin with perfection. It began with trying, falling, getting upset and coming back again.
paragraphs: Simone Biles has spent years being measured by medals, difficulty scores and the boundaries she has pushed in gymnastics. On National Gymnastics Day, she chose to highlight something far simpler: the little girl who was still learning how to put a routine together.

Biles shared some of her oldest gymnastics videos, showing early attempts that were far removed from the precision fans now associate with her. The clips included falls, awkward landings and visible frustration, accompanied by a message aimed at young athletes.

“Kids, don’t ever give up on your dreams, this is where I started… happy national gymnastics day,” Biles wrote. Another clip came with a more playful caption: “*salutes, *picks wedgie, *falls, *pout, *picks wedgie again, *stomps off.”
The humor gave the post much of its charm. One of the greatest gymnasts ever was reminding people that her journey started with the same imperfections familiar to almost every child learning a sport.
From beginner to global star
Biles first encountered gymnastics at age six during a daycare field trip to a gym. What began as an introduction soon became a serious pursuit.
She qualified for the Women’s Junior Olympic National Championships in 2010, moved into elite competition the following year and, by 2013, had won the world all-around title in Antwerp at just 16.
That breakthrough began one of the most remarkable runs in gymnastics history.

Biles collected world titles through 2014 and 2015 before making her Olympic debut in Rio in 2016. She left those Games with four gold medals, team, all-around, vault and floor exercise, plus bronze on balance beam.
Her medal total eventually reached 11 at the Olympics, with Paris 2024 providing another defining chapter as she won team, all-around and vault gold and silver on floor.
“I’m not the next Usain Bolt or Michael Phelps,” Biles famously said during her rise. “I’m the first Simone Biles.”
Message means more after difficult chapters

Biles ’ career has never been only about dominance. At the Tokyo Olympics, she withdrew from several events after experiencing the “twisties,” placing athlete mental health at the center of a global conversation.
She later returned to win bronze on balance beam before rebuilding toward another Olympic run. Her future in the sport remains open.
Biles said in 2025 that she would attend the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics whether she competed or not. By May 2026, she described the chances of another comeback as “about 50 per cent.”
“I’ve already been to three Olympic Games, and I feel fulfilled,” she said. “It’s crazy to see how people always want more and more from you. In the end, the decision will always be mine.”
That's what makes the childhood footage resonate. It shows that greatness did not begin with perfection. It began with trying, falling, getting upset and coming back again.

articles.title: Simone Biles leaves her 2028 Olympic plans open as the opportunity to compete on home soil looms
articles.standfirst: With 11 Olympic medals (7 gold) to her name, Biles is the most decorated American gymnast of all time
articles.summary: With 11 Olympic medals (7 gold) to her name, Biles is the most decorated American gymnast of all time
articles.body:
The legendary gymnastics career of Simone Biles continues to captivate the sports world as the legendary champion navigates a brand-new chapter in her personal and professional life.

Currently residing temporarily in Indianapolis following a one-year contract signing by her husband, NFL safety Jonathan Owens , with the Indianapolis Colts , Biles remains the undisputed GOAT of her sport.

With an unprecedented resume featuring 11 Olympic medals , including 7 golds, alongside a staggering 30 World Championship medals , her legacy is already firmly cemented in history.

Yet, as the athletic world looks ahead, the ultimate question remains whether the 29-year-old icon will lace up her grips and make an unthinkable run toward a fourth Olympic appearance at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games .

Simone Biles Weighs the Pull of a Home Olympics in LA 2028

The constant speculation surrounding a potential comeback is not just a media narrative; it is something that actively occupies the superstar's mind, occasionally waking her up in the middle of the night as she deliberates her competitive future.

In a candid interview with The Associated Press , Biles admitted that while she does not need to rush her final choice, her internal compass is slowly leaning in a specific direction.

The allure of competing on home soil in Los Angeles during the summer of 2028 is a powerful magnet, especially with several of her former Olympic teammates, including Suni Lee , Jordan Chiles , and Jade Carey , already targeting the historic home Games.

Biles even joked about the changing landscape of longevity in elite gymnastics, noting how former UCLA standout Katelyn Ohashi returned to elite competition this summer after a staggering 13-year hiatus.

"I know athletes are going a lot longer, and I’m just like, what the hell? It’s going to be like a big reunion if I did," Biles shared. "It would be so much fun. But I still have to weigh the options."

Balancing that temptation requires confronting the brutal physical and mental realities of the sport. By the time the Olympic flame is lit at the opening ceremony across iconic Southern California venues in July 2028 , Biles will be 31 years old , a remarkably mature age for an elite gymnast.

Having spent the past two years enjoying life away from elite competition since her historic Paris campaign, where she became just the third woman to win multiple all-around gold medals , Biles remains at peace with whatever path she chooses, proving her legendary status in gymnastics is already fully secured.

articles.title: Simone Biles reveals new ‘miserable’ eczema battle months after 'almost dying' scare
articles.standfirst: The Olympics icon said she used to itch until she would bleed because of the condition.
articles.summary: The Olympics icon said she used to itch until she would bleed because of the condition.
articles.body:
S imone Biles has revealed she spent more than two years battling painful skin problems in silence, describing an experience that became so miserable she would scratch until she bled while preparing for competition. The gymnastics legend recently opened up about being diagnosed with eczema on her arms and seborrheic dermatitis on her scalp, revealing the conditions caused persistent itching and flaking that she initially struggled to understand.

TThe seven-time Olympics gold medalist said the symptoms became particularly difficult during gymnastics preparation, when she would find herself unable to ignore the irritation. Biles said she was “standing at the chalk bucket, just itching until I'm bleeding,” illustrating how severely the condition affected her performance and distracted her in a sport where concentration can be the difference between good health and serious injury. The 29-year-old eventually sought professional treatment after initially trying to manage the symptoms herself, and admits she now uses prescription medication, including a foam treatment for her scalp and cream for her arms. “Obviously, (I have) trusted professionals around me,” Biles told TODAY. “And great, great doctors, so I'm doing a lot better. “It's still an interesting road, but I am doing a lot better. I was really self-conscious of it at first, so I kind of brushed it to the side.”

Biles admits she was in denial about skin condition

Biles said the problems began with red, itchy patches on her scalp and arms, and she and her stylist initially tried over-the-counter products and oils, but the symptoms persisted before she eventually saw a dermatologist. Examined for a “dent” in her arm and received diagnoses for the two inflammatory skin conditions, and the experience also affected Biles' confidence, particularly because of the possibility that television cameras could capture the symptoms during competitions. “If people noticed on the TV,” Biles said previously via TikTok. “I didn't want them to say something before me. So I was like, I have to address this because you couldn't just avoid it. “If they zoomed in, you could probably see it. That's when I felt it was the worst. At first I was really embarrassed and ashamed. “Like I was in denial, he was in denial. I think I have motivated him in some form, and he's [Jonathan Owens] like, 'Okay, this is a normal thing. A lot of people have it.'” The revelation comes months after Biles described a separate medical emergency as an experience in which she “almost died.” Her health and future in gymnastics remain closely connected and watched as she weighs up whether to compete at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics , where she would be 31. She says the decision is “kind of in the works,” while acknowledging the appeal of competing at a home Olympics but that family plans, the physical demands of another training cycle and her motivation to return all remain factors. Biles recently attempted a double layout in the gym and was surprised by how comfortable the skill felt, hinting that her supreme talent remains with her as the tournament approaches.
